title: Motion Alarm
intro: Catch anyone sneaking past with a motion sensor, a flashing light and an alarm.

steps.title: Test the motion sensor
steps.text:
A PIR motion sensor notices the warmth of moving people and animals. When it sees movement its pin goes `HIGH` for a few seconds.

**Your task:** Run the code, open the **Serial Monitor**, then wave your hand in front of the sensor. (In the simulator, press the wave button.) It can take a minute to settle after you plug it in.
hints: Wave your whole hand slowly, about half a metre away.
The real sensor needs up to a minute to warm up.
In the simulator, click the hand button next to the sensor.
steps.success: The sensor works! Automatic doors and security lights use these.

steps.title: Light on movement
steps.text:
Join the sensor to the LED: movement turns the light on, and it goes off when everything is still.

**Your task:** fill in the blanks.
hints: The sensor's pin is `HIGH` when it sees movement.
When there's movement, the LED should be on.

checks.label: The LED lights up when I wave

steps.success: A security light! The sensor decides, your code acts.

steps.title: Sound the alarm
steps.text:
Add a siren: two notes, one after the other, with the LED flashing in time. When everything is still, `noTone` makes it quiet.

**Your task:** fill in the second siren note (try 900 Hz).
hints: The second note should be different from the first, so it sounds like a siren.

checks.label: I heard the siren when I waved

steps.success: Nee-naw! Now nobody can sneak past.

steps.title: Count the intruders
steps.text: **Goal:** count each *new* visit. When movement starts, print `Intruder #1`, then `Intruder #2` next time, and so on, while the siren still sounds. One visit should only be counted once, however long it lasts.
hints: Make a counter variable above `setup()`: `int intruders = 0;`
Remember the last reading. A new visit is when it was `LOW` before and is `HIGH` now.
steps.success: Your alarm keeps score. Spotting the moment something changes is called edge detection.

outro: Your alarm catches movement and counts intruders. You read a **motion sensor**, made a siren with **tone()**, and counted only *new* movements by remembering the last reading.
stretch: Add a button to arm and disarm the alarm, with the LED showing whether it's armed.
Give people 5 seconds to leave after arming before the alarm starts watching.
Make the siren pattern your own: try a rising whoop from 400 Hz to 1200 Hz.
